content.thinking:
I need to plan this carefully in one pass, designing a Warcraft-style ancient treant around 4.6 meters tall, with root-like feet, a thick trunk body, broad gnarled shoulders, and a large crown.

I'm sketching out the skeleton hierarchy with hip and spine chain, legs, arms with twig-finger hands, and a jaw and crown branch joints, while settling on world-coordinate orientation conventions. I'm also defining a hand-painted warm bark and moss color palette with amber glow accents for the final look.

Writing bark paint logic...

Still building bark textures...

I'm setting up a bark helper function and defining paint variants for trunk, limb, root, and face wood with slightly different seeds. Now I'm sketching the treant skeleton in model space—hip and knee positions for stout root-like legs, planning limb chains with catmull curves for the leg joints.

For the feet, I'm building wide flattened root-foot lumps with toe roots branching off as individual chains parented to the ankle, using catmull paths for each digit.

Working out foot pad placement...

Now sketching the toe geometry as tapering tube sweeps from the foot to narrow tips, checking that each segment's radius keeps the bottom edge just above floor level.

I'm wiring up the toe chains so each digit attaches to the leg's last joint (the ankle tip), pulling it dynamically from the joints array rather than hardcoding an index.

Now I'm sweeping the leg geometry with tapering radii from hip to ankle and adding bark-colored knobs and root bulges, then building out the spine chain as a catmull-rom path from hips up through the chest with named segments for later attachment points.

Actually I'll bind the loft to both hips and spine joints, letting stations near the pelvis attach to hips and the rest follow the spine chain, with duplicate-span filtering handling any overlap at the shared start point.

For the torso cross-sections, I'm laying out stations from pelvis up through chest to the shoulder girdle and neck base, widening and deepening progressively (adding forward z-offset to simulate chest and shoulder bulge) before tapering back in at the neck.

Now adjusting the spine chain to extend to y3.3 so the loft path aligns properly, then building a short neck chain of 2-3 points branching from the chest/spine tip, parented to the spine's final joint.

Pulling the parent joint from the spine's joint array, I'm placing a head joint aimed slightly down and forward, then adding a jaw joint beneath it for a big craggy head shape.

Now I'm sketching the skull geometry: a scaled sphere for the head mass, a heavy brow ridge, a knobby branch-like nose jutting forward, and deep dark eye sockets, all centered around a defined head point roughly 0.7 wide and 0.75 tall.

I'm adding glowing amber spheres for the eyes, a frustum-shaped upper muzzle, and a bearded lower jaw built from a moss-and-root sweep along the jawbone, with a dark mouth cavity and small bone-colored tusk pegs jutting up from the chin for that chunky Warcraft-style silhouette. On top I'm planning a crown of branching antlers with jointed sweeps ending in leafy card clusters, feeding into a larger canopy overhead.

Working out the branch and leaf structure now -- deciding between six main crown branches each carrying about 25 leaf cards, with green veined leaf textures and an orange autumn variant, while figuring out whether to build the branches via a surface-hit helper or explicit chain paths with parent joints, and whether to tag them with a role like "tentacle" or leave the role unset since the standard options don't quite fit antler branches.

For the sweep along each branch, I'll compute leaf placement frames myself using the sweep's `at(t, angle)` method rather than relying on an unclear `along` callback, since that gives predictable outward-facing frames to lean the leaf cards against. Writing SVG leaf code...

For the moss, I'm drawing a hanging tuft texture as a narrow 32x64 svg with several blade-like strands, and keeping tri counts manageable by limiting card bend segments. I'm now sketching out the arm rig joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist) and their rough rest-pose coordinates for a bent arm shape.

Settling on a pose with arms angled slightly outward and down, hands open with splayed fingers — building each hand as a palm plus five digit chains (four fingers and a thumb), each with two joints, giving 20 joints total across both hands. Working out palm position and scale relative to the wrist, then planning finger base points extending outward from the palm.

Still working out hand coordinates...

I'm giving the treant long reaching arms that taper from a thick 0.3 shoulder radius down to a 0.17 wrist, with a massive moss-covered burl pauldron at the shoulder joint decorated with moss patches and mushrooms.

Now I'm placing bracket fungi on the shoulders, including a red-capped mushroom with cream spots, and draping roots across the chest using a curved sweep. I'm also thinking about adding Warcraft-style details like worn wooden trims with bronze rivets and a glowing amber rune carved into the chest, night-elf style.

I'm planning the glowing rune decal placement on the torso's front surface, with transparency so it reads as an etched glow. I also want a hollow at the chest center holding a dark recess with a glowing amber crystal "heart," wrapped in a small ring of roots.

For the back, I'm thinking of heavier bark texture and large branches emerging upward toward a canopy, giving the figure a treant-like crown.

I'm placing crown and shoulder branches with leaf clusters parented off the chest joint, aiming for the tallest point near 4.6-4.7m so the overall figure clearly towers over a human, roughly in line with something like a Warcraft Ancient Protector scale.

Now I'm working out the hip-to-leg chain: pelvis width sets hip joints at ±0.42, with knees and ankles stepping down to stout, short leg proportions suitable for a heavy treant build, and the torso loft starting around pelvis bottom. I'm detailing the bark texture on the legs with root-like buttress spikes flaring out at the base.

Rather than a loincloth, which doesn't suit a treant, I'm considering draping an ivy vine diagonally across the torso from shoulder to hip, computing its path along the body's cross-sectional ellipse, plus moss mottling near the lower legs where they'd meet mossy ground.

Writing vine and belt sweep code...

Confirming the hip loop targets the torso surface specifically, since the plane at that height also crosses the legs. For the belt, I'm picturing a woven rope or braided vine style with a bronze clasp and amber gem centered at the front.

For placement, I'll use the surface's nearest-point method rather than a ray, since that always returns a valid hit and avoids null-checking headaches — good for positioning any accessories. Thinking about additional Warcraft-style details for the treant: bronze cuffs with rivets on the arms, giving it that carved, ornamented look.

Placing the loop near the arm's tangent point rather than the exact joint, then sweeping it into a bronze tube for the wrist band.

For rivets, I'm attaching small gold spheres at points along the loop path using along/part helpers so each sphere inherits proper bone weighting. Now I'm moving on to the mushroom cap, starting a lathe profile for its shape.

Writing lathe profile...

For the stem and cap, I'm planning a helper function that builds a rod stem and lathes a cap on top with painted spots for color variation, then considering flat lathe discs for bracket fungus on the trunk.

Burls become irregularly scaled spheres stuck onto the trunk, hands get a palm sphere with fingers as clawed sweeps, and feet get three front toes plus a heel root.

Now I'm placing the eyes as glowing amber spheres set into dark hollow sockets, with a heavy brow ridge above formed from a curved tube sweep across the forehead.

For the head structure, I'm defining a cranium as a scaled sphere and building the face/muzzle region using a frustum box shape that tapers forward from a wider base to a narrower front, establishing the overall skull proportions.

I'm continuing with the facial details: a forward-pointing spike for the nose with a knot bump, cheekbone spheres positioned symmetrically, dark eye socket indentations, and glowing eye spheres placed slightly forward to catch light, before moving on to brow sweeps and ear placement.

For the mouth, I'm skipping elf-like ears for simple spikes instead, and defining the jaw structure — a lower jaw joint connecting to a jutting chin sphere, with a dark interior box standing in for the mouth cavity and plans for tusk-like upper teeth.

Still adjusting jaw and muzzle positioning...

Placing the head bone and defining neck taper with a leafy ruff, then working out antler branch positions symmetrically from the head, capping height around 4.8 units.

Now I'm sketching three antler chains per side (A, B, C) plus a central spire, each a three-point sweep anchored to the head, and figuring out how to sprout sub-twigs from arbitrary points along those sweeps using a frame-based attachment with zero-count riders.

Still refining the twig helper...

Actually, offsetting to a plain Vector3 loses the bone weighting and risks snapping to the wrong joint, so I'll just keep the frame as the base without burying it. For leaves, I'm planning to place cards on frames along each branch sweep, using randomized lean and flow values oriented outward from the sweep normal.

For canopy foliage, I'm settling on a flow direction that tilts leaves up and outward depending on frame orientation, with lean around 60 and some bend. I also want branch-tip leaf clumps scattered as small spherical clusters of cards.

For clumps, I'm using rings of cards around branch tips instead, placing frames with a small radius and tilt angle so they fan out like tufts, anchoring to the nearest joint near each tip.

Tallying up the card budget: ring clumps across branches plus along-branch leaf frames land around 600 total cards, counting moss and shoulder foliage. Now I'm thinking through how vines on the arms could spiral around using arm points with an offset catmull path.

Computing vine spline points along the arm chain, using normal and binormal vectors to offset each point into a circle at a tapering radius. I'll skin the vine path to the arm's bone chain for smooth deformation rather than assigning per-joint weights manually.

Now I'm sketching leaf cards framed along the vine path, then setting up a Warcraft-style painted shading scheme that mixes light and dark tones based on surface normal direction. Writing bark and moss texture paints...

Still writing shading logic...

I'm also adding height-based dirt and moss blending near the base, and thinking through texel resolution tradeoffs for the paint texture size given the tree's surface area — aiming for roughly 1024px with texel density around 9mm to balance detail against bake cost.

For the face, I'll use a woodPaint variant with lighter plates for the skin-like surface. For glowing elements, I'm deciding where to place emissive features—eyes, heart crystal, runes, circlet gem—and considering whether to add small floating glowing spore-motes or firefly-like orbs near the shoulders as optional guardian touches.

I'm deciding to skip the toon-style glow since the aesthetic is Blizzard hand-painted rather than cel-shaded, so I'll avoid importing a stylized glow helper. Setting up imports...

Building the skeleton hierarchy...

Still defining the neck and head joints...

Right, three points for shoulder, elbow, wrist with the arm naming by side using L/R suffix based on sign of s. Checking the arm sweep radii against shoulder placement, I notice the shoulder joint sits just outside the torso girth, so there's a slight overlap to account for where the arm sphere meets the torso.

I'm adding a shoulder burl sphere to cover that joint cleanly, then working out the arm path through shoulder, elbow, and wrist control points, checking the resulting segment lengths look proportional. With the hand and fingers extending further, the full arm reaches down near the knees on this 4.8m creature, giving it that long-limbed treant look, which feels right.

Now I'm defining the finger chain parented to the wrist joint, spreading four fingers across the x-axis with varying fan offsets and lengths so the middle finger reads longest, and setting up their curl forward in z from a base palm position.

Still defining finger geometry...

Placing the wristband near the end of the arm sweep around t=0.86. Now I'm setting up the leg bone chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, defining their path positions and sweep radii that taper down toward the ankle with a rounded cap, plus adding a knee burl sphere for the joint bump.

Building the foot pad geometry and toe placement...

I'll add a dark claw tip and a heel root path with its own radii falloff, then set up naming for the toe and heel bone chains. Tallying the full skeleton, I count 6 leg joints, 12 toe joints, 4 heel joints, 6 arm joints, and 5 finger joints.

Continuing the count, digits add up to 20 joints, plus spine, neck, head, jaw and hip joints, and roughly 7 crown branch chains with their own joints and twig/leaf details, keeping the total under 160. I'm defining the crown chains with mirrored branch types and a center branch, then adding back and shoulder foliage chains sweeping from the chest into a canopy shape for a good top-down silhouette.

For the torso, I'm planning paint details and a long list of scattered detail objects aiming for hundreds of parts: belly burls stuck onto the torso surface using random scattering with minimum distance and height filters, moss patches scattered on shoulder and top burl surfaces, and vertical bark ridge sweeps running down the torso back using angle-based path generation.

Working out the angle convention for the ridge sweep path, I'm reasoning that angle 0 corresponds to the back side of the tube for an upward-running bone, so I can place symmetrical ridges at various angles and put the main spine ridge along angle 0 on the back.

For the bone binding, I realize a single sweep path only grabs weights from the first bone it hits, which would wrongly rigidize the whole ridge to the hips -- I need to pass an explicit bone list like [hips, spine] so the ridge weights span correctly across the chain, especially since the torso isn't in rest pose during the flex test. For the dorsal spike plates along the back, I'm setting up a loop that walks along the back line and places spikes at each point, using the tangent direction rather than the outward normal to orient them.

Now I'm working out the thorn placement using sweep frames along the torso centerline, stepping t from 0.15 to 0.9 and planting spikes with length/radius scaling and bark coloring, adding some randomized variation for a more organic thorn look -- plus deciding where mushroom clusters go (shoulders, knees, back). For the chest heart-window feature, I'm calculating the torso surface depth at different y-stations to figure out where to carve or place a dark recessed ellipsoid patch that reads as a hollow rather than a protrusion.

I'm placing a glowing heart core embedded slightly in front of that hollow, plus a torus of roots encircling it so the ring sits half-buried in the surface, and sketching a rune-ring decal with eight glyph marks to project onto the chest around the heart glow, sizing it so the rune ring sits just outside the root torus.

Now I'm figuring out smaller rune decals for the shoulders, thighs, and forearms, reusing a single-glyph texture and working out the projection direction for the forearm decal so it faces outward and forward along the limb's curve.

Good, confirming a Hit works as the `at` point since it carries a normal for direction. I'll apply the same approach for thigh runes using a `runeOn` helper, and wrapping the decal in glow should work fine since it returns a Part.

I'm designing the rune SVGs now: a ring with amber stroke, glyph marks placed radially using rotation and translation, sized so strokes stay visible, plus a simpler single-glyph variant. I'm also planning glowing eye spheres and starting to define texture constants for the leaf glow.

Writing SVG code...

Drawing moss strand paths...

Skipping flowers and fireflies for now. I'm setting up a helper that generates leaf frames along a branch sweep, reusing the stick-and-card approach for foliage placement.

Writing foliage helper code...

Setting flow to the growth direction so cards curl toward the branch, giving that tip-leaf bouquet look with a slight bend for natural splay.

For moss hanging I'm defining frames at the beard, shoulders, and branch undersides, facing outward and downward so the moss droops naturally from those collection points.

I'm also thinking through arm moss placement using underside frames along the sweep, plus I still need to account for vines and bulging root shapes around the lower torso and bark ridge detailing on the trunk.

Setting up color palette and geometry helpers...

Defining wood paint textures...

I'm defining paint variants for trunk, limbs, head, roots, and crown with different wood seeds and moss amounts, plus a flat-colored twig style and a spotted mushroom cap texture. Now I'm starting the actual builder function, setting up the random seed and a sphere geometry helper to begin constructing the tree's body parts.

Writing skeleton chains...

I need to watch the cap shape at the torso's top and bottom extremes — the rounded cap radius could balloon into an oversized dome near the pelvis and neck. I'm adjusting the taper stations so the top narrows more gradually toward the shoulders, avoiding an unwanted bulge where the neck sweep meets it.

For torso details, I'm scattering belly burls using filtered surface hits (favoring the lower-front area past y=1.7), sticking small deformed spheres embedded into the skin with partial scaling, then moving on to add a back ridge feature.

I'm plotting a vine sash that drapes diagonally across the chest from shoulder to hip, repositioning its control points so the curve skirts around the heart ornament rather than overlapping it, then draping and sweeping it as a thin vine tube along bone-weighted geometry.

Now I'm setting up the heart's bone attachment to the spine chain, then moving into the arm-building loop, defining shoulder/elbow/wrist chains with named joints and sweeping tapered limb geometry with bark ridge details along each arm.

Adding spiral vine geometry...

For leaves I'll keep them small along the vine sweep, then add a wrist band using a loop cut on the arm surface at t=0.9 with a bronze ring sweep, anchored to a specific arm joint for skin weighting.

Then I'm adding gold rivets distributed along that loop path using a sphere scaled down, plus a second smaller ring near 0.82, before moving on to shape the shoulder pauldron with a scaled sphere.

For the shoulder, I'm scattering moss tufts across the burl surface using upward-facing filtered points, with a tuft texture where blades converge at the base, applying lean and cross-card rendering for volume.

Now for mushrooms on the shoulder, I'm picking the first few hits from that scatter and growing a stem outward along each surface normal. I need to figure out the right type to use for passing hit/frame data into the mushroom function, checking whether Hit is properly exported from the surface module versus using FrameInput from math.

Writing cap lathe profile...

I'm checking whether I should attach the lathe at a bone-relative position by using the frame's moved method to shift the tip point while preserving the same bone weighting.

For cap coloring, I'll use spots with red and cream paint at a small size and moderate amount for texture.

Thinking through `rod`, I confirm its signature takes two frame endpoints with radius and color arguments, so a rod from the eye to tip riding the eye's bone works as `b.rod(on, tip, [...], MUSH_CREAM)`. Now I'm considering lathe options and how color factors in there.

For bracket fungi on the trunk, I'm sketching a `shelf` helper using a hemisphere geometry stuck onto the frame — since a hemisphere's pole naturally points outward along the axis, the dome bulges out and the flat base sits against the bark, giving something like a flattened fungus cap or button rather than a true horizontal shelf. I'll approximate with a squashed scale and partial embedding so these read as fungus discs colored distinctly from the bark.

Moving to the head, I'm defining the cranium and muzzle as separate parts using a frustum-box sweep for the snout and spherical geometry for the skull, both tagged to the head bone with a shared wood paint material. I'm working through the brow ridge as a swept catmull-rom path and starting on the eye sockets with a small dark scaled sphere to suggest recessed detail.

I'm checking the geometry overlap carefully — the eye positions need to sit within the muzzle's end volume near the top corner, so I'm tracing through the box dimensions at that z-depth to confirm the sockets are properly embedded rather than floating outside the mesh.

Checking the muzzle doesn't exceed the cranium's bounds - top reaches 4.4 which stays within the cranium sphere's extent, that's fine. But the muzzle at y 3.89 with top at 4.05 overlaps where the eyes sit at y 4.0, so the eyes risk being partially covered by the muzzle's top surface.

Reworking the eye placement: moving them up to y 4.1 and solving the cranium surface position at that height gives z≈.87, placing the eye around [±.2, 4.12, .86]. Recomputing the muzzle's top edge at that z gives roughly 4.04, so the eye sits just .08 above the muzzle surface minus its radius, leaving it mostly visible rather than buried.

I'm placing the brow as a curved path above the eyes with radius .07, covering roughly 4.15-4.35 vertically, which clears the eye tops at 4.155 nicely, so I'll just nudge the cranium center up to y 4.0 to make everything fit.

That puts the head spanning from the jaw around y 3.55 up to the crown near 4.4+, giving roughly 0.9m height and 0.88m width -- reasonable proportions. I'm setting the branch roots at y 4.3-4.4 and adjusting the crown path points so the tree tops out around 5m total, which fits the Warcraft treant scale I'm going for, maybe 5.2m with leaves. Now I'm defining the nose as a spike jutting forward from around y 4.0 to a tip near y 3.82, z 1.2.

Writing spike and spline code...

Setting the tusk base height, adding a mouth interior box, and sketching beard root strands hanging from the chin as curved paths with tapering radii.

Now I'm making the beard tendrils rigid to the jaw bone, keeping about five hanging strands with moss accents positioned in front of the chest. I'm also planning a bronze circlet band wrapped around the cranium using a surface loop at a fixed height.

I realize the circlet would sit right where it overlaps the brow at y 4.2, so I'm raising it to y 4.3 to clear the brow, recalculating the cranium radius at that height to about 0.32.

I'll add an amber glow gem on the front of the circlet, positioning it near the forehead and adjusting the loop placement and sweep radius slightly to fit.

Checking the cranium geometry: at radius .36 from top, the circlet ring sits like a cap rim at roughly .25 wide, with crown branches growing inward from that ring using a tapering radius for the chains.

I'm defining three crown chain variants (A, B, C) plus a center branch, each sweeping outward and upward from the head with tapering radii, named by chain key and side. I'm also adding a back branch rooted at the chest with its own taper, plus small twig branches off the shoulder burls, and leaves scattered across all of them -- this should fit within scope.

Now I'm setting up imports (THREE, builder, frame, math helpers, path/paint utilities, glow, sweep types) and planning to keep the SVG bark/leaf textures generated inside the build function for determinism rather than at module scope, then starting to write a helper that attaches foliage onto a sweep segment.

I'm defining a `leafOn` helper that samples frames along a sweep interval with randomized offsets and spins, feeding them into the card-placement builder with size, lean, bend, flow, and variance parameters, while also thinking through whether `SweepPoint` satisfies the `Frame`/`FrameInput` type expected by `cards()` so the TypeScript types line up correctly.

Now I'm sketching a `clump` function that builds a small ring of frames around a point and renders cards on them with similar styling parameters, confirming the ring's returned items satisfy the Frame interface. Then I move on to planning the crown-building loop, iterating over sides and shape definitions to generate catmull-rom chains parented to the head object.

I'm thinking through sequencing concerns: since parts like torso lofts depend on bones existing beforehand, I need to make sure each chain is created before anything references its bones, though literal-coordinate parts with explicit bone names can be interleaved more freely. For the center crown piece, I'm defining its path points and bone names explicitly, then planning to add small twig details along the sweep at a few parametric positions.

Writing twig helper function...

Still writing torso geometry...

Adding fine burl scatter for texture, then working out the trapezius sweep connecting neck base to shoulder over the torso, figuring out which bone should drive that deformation since it spans the chest and shoulder joints.

Now I'm setting up the leg sweep geometry with tapering radii, and adding buttress-like ridge sweeps running down the thigh at flanking angles, plus a kneecap burl sphere, all bound to the leg bone chain.

Then I'm placing moss tufts around the ankle using frame positions along the leg path, plus a bronze rivet band looping around the leg at a fixed point for detail.

For the feet, I'm scattering grass tufts near the ankle bone rigged to the feet and heels, with randomized sizes and positions to make it look like standing in grass—skipping flowers for now to keep it simple.

Moving to hands, I'm building four finger chains with curved catmull paths tapering by length, swept with a rounded profile for the palm pad, and adding claw spikes at the fingertips.

Fingers should stay spread apart, with knuckle spheres and bark rings for texture. The leg chain ends at the ankle joint, with feet and toes built off that joint, while the arm skeleton follows a similar forward clustering approach.

Roughly tallying parts now: torso elements (loft, ridges, thorns, burls, belt, buckle, heart, sash, trapezius, runes) come to about 55, each leg adds up to around 28 (sweep, ridges, knee burl, bands with rivets, foot, toes, heel, tufts), and arms are shaping up similarly with sweep, ridges, vine, banded rivets, burls, moss, and mushrooms—aiming for roughly 400 parts total.

Head, crown with chains and twigs, and back branches each add their own chunks, with mushroom and moss textures scattered across the body and limbs. I'm mentally checking that catmull sweeps for Vector3 paths will work correctly with bone references like the head joint, and confirming the radius arrays for tapering elements like the beard will produce the right thickness falloff with rounded caps.

I'm verifying torso.line's signature takes angle and lift to build paths, that surface sweeps target correctly, and that scatter returns Hit objects with position and normal data filtered by a boolean predicate. For burl coloring I'll reuse the bark palette with flat paint rather than introducing new materials, keeping things simple. I'm also setting up a glowing amber heart element using an icosahedron attached to a spine joint with flat shading enabled.

Now I'm working through the rune ring decal placement on the torso, confirming the decal system handles its own textured material separately from paint so glow still applies correctly, then extending that to eye glow and smaller rune decals on the forearm and thigh using nearest-surface lookups to position them accurately along the limb paths.

Writing SVG code...

I need to check the transform order—rotate applied after translate since SVG reads rightmost first. The glyph sits at radius 42, positioned between the two circles at radius 46 and 33, so I should adjust the translate distance to fit properly within that band.

I'll settle on defining four simple symbol glyphs with ±4 amplitude (small stroke-based shapes for the compass points), leaving the center open for a heart shape.

Now I'm sketching a larger single compass glyph at a bigger scale, then moving on to design leaf, tuft, and moss elements—grass blade paths with varied green fills, and a hanging moss piece rooted near the bottom of its viewBox.

Still writing styles...

Then I think through how moss card frames hang with lean and orientation vectors, and start mentally assembling the full file, watching for TypeScript strictness issues like unused locals and how to properly type the chain object returned from the builder, deciding to import the Chain type directly from the skeleton module instead of declaring a local alias.

Writing texture and leaf generator code...

Still writing leaf SVG...

Now I'm sketching a mushroom generator function that builds a rod stem with a lathe-shaped cap, adding spots and color variation based on a seed.

I'm checking whether the outline point arrays get properly typed when passed inline versus stored in a variable, since literal arrays might widen to plain number[][] instead of the expected tuple type—plus double-checking that the frame's moved() call accepts the Vector3 I'm passing in.

Now I'm sketching out the shelf fungus function, using a partial sphere geometry scaled non-uniformly to create a bracket shape, and confirming the stick helper's scale parameter accepts a vector. Moving on to the torso and tusks, then verifying the catmull-rom chain path accepts the array-of-arrays point format I'm feeding it.

Writing per-side leg chains...

Now I'm adding an ankle band with a bronze sweep and small gold studs placed along the loop, checking that the callback signature for placing parts along the path works correctly.

I'm confirming the loop is anchored at the right point along the leg chain, with rivets carrying proper skin weights, then moving on to build the toes—setting up a forEach loop over three offsets to generate symmetric toe paths with distinct start and end points for each.

I'm checking that the toe offsets don't let inner toes cross the midline between feet, adjusting the multipliers so the fan spreads correctly, then setting the per-toe radii to taper from thick at the root to thin at the tip.

Still working out the claw spikes attached to each toe tip, orienting them along the tangent so they angle down slightly as they'd naturally rest on the floor, and now I'm defining the heel root path and its radii.

Then I'm adding ground tuft cards anchored rigidly to the ankle bone, and setting up the arm chain with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints, reconsidering whether to parent it to the chest or to a specific spine joint so the shoulder height lines up correctly.

Working out sweep radii and ridge angles for the arm, plus adding wrist and elbow details, spiraling moss vines along the limb, and hanging moss cards from frames anchored under the forearm before moving on to the shoulder burl detail.

For the shoulder burl, I'm scattering points across its surface with a minimum distance filter favoring upward-facing normals, then assigning the first few hits to mushrooms of varying size and the remainder to moss tufts with some lean and random variation.

I'm also planning small twig sprouts from remaining hits using a shared helper that builds a spike frame and clumps leaves at the tip, trying to unify the twig logic so it works consistently from either a surface hit or a sweep frame.

Now I'm moving on to the jaw geometry and head structure, then crown and back builds afterward. I'm also setting up texture arrays grouping the leaf variants for use across the crown and canopy.

Sizing the crown leaves a bit larger for a denser canopy mass, then sanity-checking the card/triangle counts for the crown chains to make sure the polygon budget stays reasonable. I'm also scattering burls on the torso parts, picking from the bark color variants for each stick.

Placing thorns along the torso back (using the loft's clock convention so they land correctly rather than on the front/chest), then adding a belt loop at the hips with a rope sweep and bronze buckle, choosing fiber-rope coloring over leather or vine.

For the buckle gem, I'm finding the nearest frame hit at the front of the chest and stacking a bronze cylinder with a glowing amber octahedron slightly less embedded so it protrudes as a gem above the button's surface, working out the embed depths so the gem sits just above the sunk button.

I'm skipping extra belt plates and chest carving details for now and moving to defining the head bones, writing eye sockets and glowing amber pupils on the head using scaled spheres positioned symmetrically on both sides.

Now I'm figuring out the rotation angle to give the eyes an angry slitted tilt, working out that outer corners should rotate upward and inner corners downward, matching the brow slant for a consistent angry expression.

I'm adding a tiny highlight sphere for the eye core, then double-checking the head, neck, and chest proportions to make sure the cranium, neck joint, and shoulder width all connect smoothly without clashing.

The head reads a bit small compared to the shoulders, so instead of scaling the whole figure up, I'll just enlarge the cranium radii directly to give it a bit more presence, while keeping the muzzle width proportional.

With the cranium resized, I recheck eye, cheek, and brow placements to make sure they still land correctly on the new surface, and confirm the crown dome and branch roots sit properly inside the enlarged skull. I'm ready to write out the full final code now, including the exported meta data.

Writing branch helper function...

Naming branch endpoints with unique suffixes, then writing a decorate helper that adds leaf clusters and computes direction vectors from the branch's sweep points...

I'm fixing the Vector3 construction to use fromArray instead of spreading, since TS flags array spreads into constructors; then placing twigs at a few points along the branch with randomized angles, blending each twig's outward axis with the branch direction for a natural splay.

I'm now tallying up the full skeleton: counting chains for arms, legs, toes, fingers, crown, back, spine, and neck, then adding up their joints to make sure the rig totals are consistent across hips, head, jaw, fingers, and heels.

I'm checking overall proportions — adjusting the crown tip height so the total figure stays around 5.2 meters, and verifying feet, toes, and head positions don't overlap, plus confirming leg and arm stance widths look balanced for an ancient protector figure.

Now I'm drafting a helper for hanging moss clusters using card frames with randomized spin and flow, plus cleaning up unused variables and double-checking type signatures for the frame and card scattering functions line up correctly.

I'm checking the nearest-point calculation for leg decals, confirming the glyph decal placement and sizing, and verifying the final return statement and paint definitions for crown, limb, and head materials, along with the socket sphere's position and dimensions.

Now I'm positioning the heart socket on the torso surface, checking protrusion depth so the dark ellipse and glowing icosahedron are visible, and adding a bark-colored torus ring plus a smaller bronze accent ring around the gem area.
